properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Potrero Power Station Design for Development's own Figure 6.2.3 (Building Height Plan, p.245) -- an adopted regulatory diagram with a printed scale bar, north arrow, and real street labels (Illinois St, Georgia St, Louisiana St, Maryland St, Delaware St, 22nd St, Humboldt St, 23rd St), not an illustrative rendering. Georeferenced using 9 real street-intersection control points fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py, fit as a least-squares affine transform. NOTE: an initial attempt also used the real, confirmed positions of the Sophie Maxwell Building and the UCSF Block 2 building as anchors, but they produced 50-60m of error against the street-only fit -- this diagram is dated Feb 26, 2020, predating UCSF's ~2023-24 arrival as a life-science anchor tenant, so those two real buildings likely do not sit where this 2020 figure's own numbered blocks would place them (their own real parcels are used directly elsewhere in this dataset and were NOT re-derived from this diagram). The final transform here uses street intersections only. Residual error against those control points is roughly 8-24m. Traced polygons were additionally clipped against the real, confirmed Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels (and against Prequel Park's approximate geometry) so this speculative tracing never overrides real or better-sourced geometry. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (first pass, superseded): user-flagged check of this block's south edge found the SW corner sitting directly on top of a real existing building's roof, well south of 23rd Street. Since the yard here has no visible dirt/pavement curb to measure, used the building's own roofline (measured at two points 33m apart) as a hard constraint, with a 3m clearance -- this only guaranteed no more building overlap, not that the edge sat at the street's true curb. SECOND PASS: user re-flagged the block as still eating the street even after that fix. Went back to the source diagram (Figure 6.2.3) and measured it directly against its own printed scale bar -- this block's own north-south depth (from its shared boundary with Power Station Park to 23rd Street) is roughly 100px at the diagram's ~0.99px/ft scale, i.e. about 31m. This block's committed depth (north edge to first-pass south edge) was 66-67m, more than DOUBLE the diagram's own dimension -- meaning the original diagram-transform trace was badly wrong in an entirely different way than the curb question (a shape/scale error, not just a position error), and no amount of satellite curb-hunting on the south edge could have fixed it, since the real problem was the block being stretched roughly 2x too deep in the first place. Rebuilt the south edge by keeping the (unmodified, more trustworthy) north edge corners fixed and moving south exactly 30.8m along the established 356.5 deg grid bearing, matching the diagram's own measured depth. Note: this block's WIDTH also disagrees with the diagram (currently ~55m vs a diagram-implied ~92m) -- NOT corrected in this pass since it would require moving the east or west edge (shared boundaries with other features not re-verified here); flagged as a known follow-up. CORRECTED 2026-09-16: user-flagged pattern of blocks encroaching on real streets across the site (Block 3, Block 11, Block 12) led to rebuilding this whole block layer from scratch using proper GCP-based georeferencing (GDAL's gdaltransform with a thin-plate-spline transform, the same technique QGIS's Georeferencer uses) instead of patching individual curbs. Installed GDAL, computed 8 real street-intersection ground control points from OpenStreetMap data (Craig Lane x Maryland St, 22nd St x Maryland/Louisiana St, Humboldt St x Maryland/Delaware/Georgia Lane, 23rd St x Maryland/Georgia Lane), precisely located each in the source diagram (Figure 6.2.3) via programmatic black-pixel border detection cross-checked with visual ruler crops, and fit a TPS transform. Re-traced this block's own corner pixels the same way and ran them through the new transform. This corrected transform disagrees with the original 9-point affine transform by tens of meters in places -- e.g. it revealed the original trace had Blocks 3/4 shifted east into the excavation pit/street area, and Blocks 11/12 roughly 2x too deep -- and the new positions now land within real, distinct site features (buildings, graded lots) visible in satellite imagery rather than straddling roads. Known residual limitation: GCP street positions are centerline-based (matching OSM convention), while a block boundary should sit at the near curb, so any edge close to a GCP street can land a few meters into that street after transformation -- checked for and corrected on this block's street-facing edge(s) where applicable using this project's already-established grid bearing (356.5 deg) and, where available, an independently diagram-measured depth/width. Treat corrected vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-15m (tighter than the original 8-24m transform, but still not survey-grade). RE-CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (same day, third pass): the independent per-block TPS re-trace (see above) still measured each block's own 4 corners in isolation, which -- despite using the same transform -- left small (3-12m) spurious gaps or misalignments at boundaries the diagram actually draws as shared or tightly-spaced between adjacent blocks (caught after the user pointed out the diagram itself has ~zero wasted space and specifically that the PG&E switchyard polygon sits directly against Block 5 in the diagram, not ~60m away as this dataset had it). Re-measured EVERY block's corners in a single consistent pass using programmatic black-pixel border detection (long contiguous runs = real borders, filtered from text/dimension-arrow strokes by requiring the run to span nearly the full block height/width), cross-validated with fine-pixel-gridline crops, so that shared or consistently-measured boundaries between neighboring blocks now come from the same underlying pixel measurements rather than independent eyeball estimates. Batch-transformed through the same GDAL/TPS fit as before. This pass also corrected several block extents that were measured imprecisely in the prior pass (e.g. Block 5's real stepped/notched south edge, Block 11's true position -- it does NOT sit flush against Block 15, there is real Power Station Park open space between them). GCP CORRECTION 2026-09-16 (fourth pass): user flagged that Block 8/12 should touch Delaware Street with park space between them, and that Block 3/4's shapes looked off -- investigation found the root cause was a single mis-measured ground control point. The 'Delaware St x Humboldt St' GCP used for the whole site's TPS transform had been placed at pixel (2227, 986), which is actually deep inside Building 9's own footprint in the diagram, not on Delaware Street at all -- confirmed by comparing pixel spacing between the three Humboldt-row GCPs (Maryland/Delaware/Georgia Lane): Maryland-to-Georgia-Lane's pixel:real-world ratio implied Delaware should sit at roughly pixel x=2020, not 2227, and a direct color-transition scan at y=986 confirmed the real street gap is at x=1994-2035. Corrected the GCP to (2015, 986) (same real-world coordinate, just the right pixel) and re-ran the TPS transform for the whole site. This produced large corrections concentrated exactly where the user's complaint pointed -- Block 4 shifted 33-60m, Block 3's east corners ~28-33m, Block 8's east corners ~29-31m, Block 12's east corners ~26-27m -- while blocks far from the error (5, 15, 7, 11, PG&E) shifted well under 5m, consistent with a localized GCP error rather than a global transform problem. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source URL cited for this file (the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the D4D at default.sfplanning.org) is dead (404); the text above describes the final D4D (dated February 26, 2020), so source_doc_urls now points to potreropower_D4D_final.pdf, where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan is on printed p.245 (PDF p.247) and shows a north arrow, a scale bar (0-400 ft) and the street labels listed above. Corrections to statements above: (1) the '~2023-24 arrival' of UCSF as anchor tenant has no cited source; the dated source found is the UC Regents' September 2024 CEQA findings (Attachment 6), which state that in 2024 the City approved an assignment and assumption agreement under which UCSF assumes a portion of the developer's rights. (2) In the final D4D's Figure 6.2.3 the green strip between Block 15 and Block 11 is labelled 'LOUISIANA PASEO'; 'POWER STATION PARK' is labelled north of Block 11, between it and Block 7. (3) Re-measured against the printed scale bar on a 300 dpi render of PDF p.247: Block 11's 130-ft fill is about 229 ft by 107 ft (roughly 70 m by 33 m), so the diagram-implied width is about 70 m, not ~92 m; the ~31 m depth above is consistent. The committed geometry was not changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (final D4D, Feb 26, 2020: Table 3.1.1 and Figure 6.2.3) -- see accuracy_caveat. Status 'planned': design under review per the 2024 annual compliance report (March 28, 2025). Use 'commercial': office, laboratory and life science uses are permitted and residential is not (D4D Table 3.1.1).'; accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (design under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report) and this approximate footprint has not been matched to an Assessor parcel: DataSF Parcels lists an active, unaddressed lot, 4232021 (recorded 2022-08-30), that overlaps about three quarters of it, but that lot has not been confirmed as this block's parcel. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade. South edge corrected 2026-09-16 (second pass) using the source diagram's own measured depth rather than a satellite curb search (see digitization_method) -- the diagram-derived depth should be reliable to within a few meters, but this edge has NOT been independently confirmed against a visible real-world curb. This block's WEST-EAST WIDTH is also known to disagree with the diagram (~55m actual vs ~70m implied by the 2026-09-29 re-measurement, originally recorded as ~92m) and has NOT been corrected -- flagged as an open follow-up, not resolved. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method.'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (design under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report) and this approximate footprint has not been matched to an Assessor parcel: DataSF Parcels lists an active, unaddressed lot, 4232021 (recorded 2022-08-30), that overlaps about three quarters of it, but that lot has not been confirmed as this block's parcel. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, fitted to the real street grid at several points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade. South edge corrected 2026-09-16 (second correction) using the source diagram's own measured depth rather than a search for the curb in satellite imagery -- the diagram-derived depth should be reliable to within a few meters, but this edge has NOT been independently confirmed against a visible real-world curb. This block's WEST-EAST WIDTH is also known to disagree with the diagram (~55m actual vs ~70m implied by the 2026-09-29 re-measurement, originally recorded as ~92m) and has NOT been corrected -- flagged as an open follow-up, not resolved. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 by fitting the diagram to surveyed reference points. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third correction) in one consistent measurement across the whole block layout. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth correction) after one mis-measured reference point was fixed. Each step is logged in this shape's data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) lists an active, unaddressed lot, 4232021 (recorded 2022-08-30, PPS-MU zoning), overlapping about three quarters of this approximate footprint; it has not been confirmed as this block's parcel.
properties.regulatory_context: Flat 130 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (the colour-coded height label). The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) shows Non-Retail Sales and Services (including office), Laboratory and Life Science uses permitted (subject to the table's note 13) and Residential not permitted here. Blocks 11 and 12 together are described as approximately 430,000 sq ft of office by the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+ Engineers project page, a consultant's own material, not a Planning document). The Meyers+ page and the June 7, 2020 pre-application community meeting slides list Herzog & de Meuron + Adamson Associates as architect for Blocks 11, 12 and 15. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (final D4D, Feb 26, 2020: Table 3.1.1 and Figure 6.2.3) -- see its accuracy caveat. Status 'planned': design under review per the 2024 annual compliance report (March 28, 2025). Use 'commercial': office, laboratory and life science uses are permitted and residential is not (D4D Table 3.1.1).
